# nonConsistent2DArray

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is not a matrix with uniform row lengths.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonConsistent2DArray() — Checks whether a value is not a matrix with uniform row lengths. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/array</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonConsistent2DArray<T>(arr: T | Array<Array<unknown>>): arr is T;
```

`nonConsistent2DArray(value)` is the same test as `!isConsistent2DArray(value)`, written so that a guard clause
reads forwards — see [](validation-conventions.md).

Like [`non2DArray`](non2DArray.md), it is best used for its boolean answer: after the check TypeScript does not
hand back a usable matrix type. [`requireConsistent2DArray`](requireConsistent2DArray.md) is what validates and
returns the matrix.

It reports `true` for two different situations: a matrix whose rows differ in length, and a value that is not a
matrix at all. They are indistinguishable from the result alone, so use [`non2DArray`](non2DArray.md) when the
difference matters.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                         | Description            |
| :-------- | :--------------------------- | :--------------------- |
| `arr`     | `T \| Array<Array<unknown>>` | Array<Array<unknown>>` |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` if the value is not a non-empty array of arrays of equal length; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `arr` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### Both failing cases

```javascript
nonConsistent2DArray([[1, 2], [3]]); // => true — ragged
nonConsistent2DArray([1, 2]); // => true — not 2D
nonConsistent2DArray([
  [1, 2],
  [3, 4]
]); // => false
```

### Telling the two apart

<tabs group="code">
<tab title="TypeScript" group-key="ts">
<code-block lang="typescript" src="nonConsistent2DArray.ts" include-symbol="describeShape"/>
</tab>
<tab title="JavaScript" group-key="js">
<code-block lang="javascript">
function describeShape(rows) {
  if (non2DArray(rows)) {
    return "not a matrix";
  }
  if (nonConsistent2DArray(rows)) {
    return "a matrix, but the rows differ in length";
  }
  return "ready for setValues";
}
</code-block>
</tab>
</tabs>
